conflicts.description: The Windward Compact wants the failing skybridges replaced by kite-lines only they can fly, which would bind every island to their monopoly; the Chartbound and Night Keepers believe the bridges can be renewed if the enclaves share their charts — a plan the Compact quietly sabotages.
conflicts.name: Chart or Chains

conflicts.description: A growing movement among the Rootwardens teaches that Aethervale was meant to drift apart and that re-binding the skybridges defies the islands' nature; if the enclaves cannot agree on whether unity is salvation or a cage, no map will hold the realm together.
conflicts.name: The Scatter Question

description: Aethervale is a fractured realm of floating islands adrift in an endless luminous sky, bound together by ancient skybridges woven from crystallized cloudlight and the will of the First Cartographers. For a thousand years these luminous spans have kept the archipelago whole, allowing trade, pilgrimage, and fragile peace among rival enclaves who remember being one people. Now the skybridges are dimming — hairline fractures spread along their spans, islands drift a finger's breadth farther apart each season, and old treaties are fraying as fast as the bridges themselves. In this wondrous but imperiled world, a young cartographer apprentices with the last true mappers of the drifting realm and discovers that the bridges are not merely old — they are failing in a deliberate pattern, as though the sky itself has begun to forget its shape. To save Aethervale, she must chart a new map of trust, uniting the proud enclaves of wind-harvesters, tide-shepherds, star-tenders, and root-farmers before the islands scatter into the unending blue. Every breeze carries pollen, birdsong, and rumor; every bridge crossing is a small act of faith. The tone is wondrous: dawn light on spun-glass spans, kites the size of ships, markets suspended between islands, and the vertiginous beauty of a world where falling is the oldest fear and connection the oldest hope.

factions.description: The guild of cartographers descended from the First Cartographers, sworn to keep the map of Aethervale updated as islands drift. They hold the only true records of skybridge health and are torn between their vow of neutrality and the need to warn the enclaves.
factions.name: The Chartbound

factions.description: A hard-bitten alliance of storm-harvesters and watchkeepers who control the upper wind lanes and the strongest tether-crystals. They believe the failing skybridges should be replaced by kite-lines only they can fly — which would make every island dependent on them.
factions.name: The Windward Compact

factions.description: Farmers, seed-keepers, and gravity-orchard tenders who physically anchor islands with living root-masses. Some factions among them preach the Scatter Gospel — that Aethervale was always meant to drift apart — and they may not be wrong.
factions.name: The Rootwardens

factions.description: Reclusive star-tenders and tide-chroniclers who maintain the drift-charts and the hidden archive of First Cartographer journals. They know the skybridges are failing by design, not age, and guard the name of the architect who wrote the unraveling.
factions.name: The Night Keepers

history.description: A thousand years ago the single landmass of Aethervale cracked into drifting islands during a cataclysm remembered only in song; survivors clung to the fragments as they scattered across the sky.
history.name: The Sundering

history.description: The First Cartographers discovered that true maps drawn in memory-ink could condense cloudlight into walkable spans, and raised the original skybridges that reunited the scattered islands.
history.name: The Weaving of the First Skybridges

history.description: After a generation of bridge tolls and skirmishes, the enclaves signed the Accord guaranteeing passage to true-chart bearers, ushering in centuries of uneasy peace.
history.name: The Accord of Seven Spans

history.description: A season in which three minor islets drifted beyond recall when their neglected skybridge failed; the enclaves blamed one another rather than the failing span, and the seeds of present rivalry were sown.
history.name: The Hollow Year

history.description: Within living memory, hairline fractures began appearing along the great spans in a deliberate spiral pattern; the Night Keepers recognized the pattern from a forbidden First Cartographer journal and sealed their archive.
history.name: The First Cracks

locations.description: The heart-isle and largest of the fragments, crowned with white-stone terraces and the Great Chart Hall where the First Cartographers' maps glow on living parchment. Lumerans trade lamplight-crystal and memory-ink, and their docks host the busiest skybridge confluence in Aethervale — the Anchor of Seven Spans.
locations.name: Lumera

locations.description: A jagged chain of wind-scoured islets where the Kestrel folk harvest storm-kites and tether-crystals that sing in high winds. Its residents breed messenger hawks and keep the oldest watch-towers, and they distrust anyone who cannot read the sky's moods.
locations.name: Kestrel Reef

locations.description: A lush green island hanging low in the cloudline, famous for root-farms that bind soil to stone and gravity-orchards whose fruit ripens while tumbling slowly through the air. The Vaelis believe the islands are seeds that wish to scatter, which puts them at odds with those who would keep Aethervale bound.
locations.name: Vaelis Gardens

locations.description: A shadowed crescent isle that drifts slightly out of phase with the others, where star-tenders collect nightlight and keep the tide-charts that predict island drift. Its libraries of dark-ink scrolls hold secrets about why the skybridges were built — and who might be unmaking them.
locations.name: Nocturne Shoal

name: Aethervale

rules.statement: Skybridges are spans of crystallized cloudlight anchored to the will and memory of living cartographers; every skybridge weakens when no one accurately charts the islands it connects.
Combustible explosive powder does not exist in Aethervale; travel, construction, and conflict rely on wind, crystal resonance, woven rope, and living root-matter.
Islands drift on currents of sky-tide; any island not bound by a skybridge or a living root-anchor will slowly wander beyond rescue within a generation.
Anything that falls from an island or bridge falls forever into the Blue Beneath; no one has ever returned, though folklore insists the Beneath has a bottom.
Maps drawn in memory-ink record not only geography but the trust between places; an accurate map strengthens the skybridge it depicts, and a falsified map can sever one.
By the Accord of Seven Spans, no enclave may deny passage across a skybridge to a bearer of a true chart, though each enclave may demand a toll in goods, songs, or secrets.
